newsitem.title: FRANCE: Zeroual says constitution in force "within days".
newsitem.headline: Zeroual says constitution in force "within days".

text.p: Algerian President Liamine Zeroual said on Tuesday that the constitutional reforms approved in last month's referendum would come into force "within days".
The constitutional changes, approved by 84.6 percent of voters, strengthen the president's powers and ban political parties based on religion, language or regionalisation.

In a speech to judges at the opening of the judicial year, reported by the official Algerian news agency APS, Zeroual said the reforms were being implemented "in the perspective of completing the electoral process".
Zeroual has promised general elections early next year.

Algeria has not had an elected parliament since January 1992 and many of the elected officers of townhalls -- controlled by Islamic fundamentalists after 1991 regional polls -- have been replaced by government appointees.

Algeria has been embroiled in a five-year-old conflict between the authorities and Moslem fundamentalists, sparked by the cancellation in January 1992 of a general election in which Islamic fundamentalists had taken a commanding lead.
Some 60,000 people have since been killed.
